# onpager_role_assignment (Resource)

Manage one native role assignment for an explicit role, recipient and target scope. Changes atomically replace the full assignment tuple while preserving its UUID and comparing its saved prior tuple.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_role_assignment" "example" {
  role_id = var.role_id
  recipient = {
    kind = "service_account"
    id   = var.service_account_id
  }
  target_team_id = var.target_team_id
}

variable "role_id" {
  description = "Existing role UUID compatible with the target scope and service-account recipient."
  type        = string
}
variable "service_account_id" {
  description = "Existing service account UUID."
  type        = string
}
variable "target_team_id" {
  description = "Target team UUID for a team role, or null for a tenant role."
  type        = string
  default     = null
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `recipient` (Attributes) Exact recipient of this role assignment. Changing its kind or UUID updates the assignment atomically. Ownership and token issuance do not create this grant implicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recipient))
- `role_id` (String) Existing role UUID. The role and its scope determine which permissions are granted. Changes update the assignment atomically while preserving its UUID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `target_team_id` (String) Target team UUID for a team-scoped role. Omission or null denotes a tenant-scoped assignment. The API validates role/target compatibility. Changes update the assignment atomically while preserving its UUID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--recipient"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recipient`

Required:

- `id` (String) Existing recipient UUID matching the selected kind. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `kind` (String) Recipient kind: `user`, `service_account`, `group` or `team`. Team and group recipients grant access through their current eligible memberships.

## Import

Import using the assignment UUID.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_role_assignment.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_role_assignment.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Lifecycle

Changing the role, recipient kind or UUID, or target scope atomically updates
the existing assignment UUID. The provider sends the complete desired tuple
and compares the complete prior tuple saved in Terraform state. The role must
support the selected target scope: tenant roles use null `target_team_id`; team
roles require an appropriate team UUID. The API validates recipient eligibility,
including service-account restrictions. Refresh records authorized UI changes to
the same UUID so a later apply can reconcile configured values.

Create ensures the exact role/recipient/target tuple and can return an existing
identical assignment. Manage each tuple once; import existing assignments before
adopting them. Protected assignments cannot be managed.

Destroy revokes only this assignment. Other assignments, defaults and
membership-derived access remain independent, so the recipient can retain access
through another source.

Assignments have no revision or `If-Match`. Updates use full-tuple comparison:
HTTP 412 reports a stale prior tuple and HTTP 409 rejects protected assignments
or a destination tuple already owned by another UUID. No assignments are merged,
and conflicts are not retried implicitly. Run a new plan after concurrent edits.

The API returns HTTP 403 for missing authority and HTTP 404 for confirmed absence
on direct reads and deletes. Failed updates retain state, including HTTP 404.
A successful update receipt populates state directly, so self-demotion needs no
follow-up read. A successful HTTP update with an invalid receipt retains its
known UUID and committed desired values with a diagnostic. A known committed
UUID is also retained if a create receipt is incomplete.

## Permissions

Requires `role_assignments.create`, `role_assignments.read` and
`role_assignments.delete` in the actual target scope. Tenant assignments require
tenant grants. An update requires delete authority in the actual old scope and
create authority in the requested new scope; there is no separate update grant.
Read permission is independent and remains necessary for Terraform refresh and
import, even when a mutation succeeds. Protected-assignment checks apply to
personal tokens and service accounts.
